title: Neighbors’ review requests and delay, by district
question: How often does the Planning Commission take discretionary review when a neighbor asks, what happens then, and how many times are projects put off in each district?
finding: The 2019-2022 minutes hold 234 requests for discretionary review: 148 were heard and review was taken in 83 (56.1%), with the permit refused in 8; 61 were withdrawn. Across 872 projects at an address, 32.8% were continued at least once - 0.67 continuances per project, from 0.41 in District 7 to 0.87 in District 11.
how: A review request is one case number with a discretionary-review suffix; its outcome is the last decisive action on it (“Took DR” and what followed, “No DR”, or withdrawn). A project is one case-number root at an address; a continuance is a hearing date on which any of its items was continued. Districts are placed by parcel or address under the 2012 lines. Planning-law items, landmark designations and legacy-business recommendations are left out of the project count. Rates are printed only on 20 or more cases.
limits: The minutes do not print who asked for a review, so requesters - neighbors, organizations, repeat filers - cannot be told apart here. A continuance can be requested by the applicant or agreed with the neighbors, and a project with several approvals appears on the calendar more than once. Review requests follow the kind of permit: the districts with the most requests are not the districts with the most projects. A difference between areas, or between groups of cases, is not proof of bias. Areas differ in what is proposed, in zoning, lot sizes, building ages and land prices, and in who chooses to apply, object or appeal at all.

columns.t: Projects continued three or more times

sources.t: San Francisco Planning Department, Planning Commission hearing archive: minutes, January 2019 to August 2022, with 1 earlier hearing in April 2018
